hansard-1923.title: Colonial Office, House of Commons debate of 25 July 1923 (HC Deb vol 167)
hansard-1923.note: The Secretary of State for the Colonies states that after the referendum the Imperial Government decided that responsible government should be set up in Southern Rhodesia on 1 October 1923, as a self-governing Colony.

hansard-1922.title: Referendum, Southern Rhodesia, written answers of 22 May 1922 (HC Deb vol 154 cc846-7W)
hansard-1922.note: The referendum on responsible government was to be put to the voters qualified to vote for the election of members of the Legislative Council.

hansard-1934.title: Sweepstakes (Referendum, Southern Rhodesia), House of Commons, 13 March 1934
hansard-1934.note: The Under-Secretary for the Dominions reports, from press reports, a referendum in Southern Rhodesia carried by 16,949 to 3,604 in favour of sweepstakes under strict legislative control, with 73 per cent of the electorate voting.

hansard-1957.title: Rhodesia and Nyasaland (Constitution), House of Commons debate of 25 November 1957
hansard-1957.note: States that the Southern Rhodesian Assembly has had only 30 members since 1923.

hansard-1961.title: Southern Rhodesia, House of Commons debate of 22 June 1961
hansard-1961.note: Debate on the 1961 constitutional proposals ahead of the Southern Rhodesian referendum on them, then a few weeks away.

hansard-1962.title: British Policy in Central Africa, House of Lords debate of 19 December 1962
hansard-1962.note: Reports the Southern Rhodesian general election of the previous week: 35 seats to the Rhodesian Front, all in European constituencies, and 29 to the United Federal Party, 14 of them won by Africans in African constituencies.

hansard-1969.title: Rhodesia, House of Commons statement of 24 June 1969
hansard-1969.note: The Foreign and Commonwealth Secretary comments on the results of the referendum held in Rhodesia on 20 June 1969.

hansard-1979.title: Rhodesia, House of Lords debate of 10 July 1979
hansard-1979.note: The 1979 constitution was endorsed by a referendum of the white electorate (over 71 per cent turnout, 84 per cent in favour), and the elections of April 1979 led to a new Government under Bishop Muzorewa at the end of May.

hansard-1980.title: Rhodesia Elections: New Government, House of Lords statement of 4 March 1980
hansard-1980.note: Lord Carrington gives the results of the Common Roll elections announced that morning (ZANU(PF) 57 seats, Patriotic Front 20, UANC 3) and the Election Commissioner's report to the Governor.

ipu-1980.title: Zimbabwe: parliamentary elections of February 1980 (Chronicle of Parliamentary Elections XIV, 1979-80)
ipu-1980.note: House of Assembly elections of 14 February 1980 (20 White Roll seats, 14 unopposed) and 27-29 February 1980 (80 Common Roll seats in eight electoral districts by party list), the Senate of 19 March 1980 chosen by electoral colleges, and independence on 18 April 1980; national totals of electors, voters, and votes by party.

zimbabwe-act.title: Zimbabwe Act 1979 (c. 60), as enacted
zimbabwe-act.note: Section 1: on Independence Day, appointed by Order in Council, Southern Rhodesia becomes an independent Republic under the name of Zimbabwe.

classes.finest_note: Constituency (electoral district); no official return is online.
classes.note: Thirty members from 1924 to 1958 on a qualified, in practice largely European, roll. The 1961 Constitution raised the Assembly to 65 members: 50 constituencies and 15 electoral districts, with A and B rolls and cross-voting, first used in December 1962. The Rhodesian Front won 35 seats in 1962 and every seat on the A roll in 1965. Unilateral independence was declared on 11 November 1965 and the Legislative Assembly sat until the republican Parliament of 1970.

classes.finest_note: Constituency for the European (White Roll) seats; electoral district for the 1979 and 1980 Common Roll party-list seats.
classes.note: The 1969 Constitution (republic from 2 March 1970) gave a 66-member House: 50 European-roll constituencies, 8 African-roll seats elected directly, and 8 chosen by electoral colleges of chiefs, headmen, and councillors (elections of 1970, 1974, and 1977). The 1979 Constitution of Zimbabwe Rhodesia gave 100 seats, 72 Common Roll seats by party list in eight electoral districts, 20 White Roll constituencies, and 8 further white members; the White Roll polled on 10 April and the Common Roll from 17 to 21 April 1979. Under the British Governor the election of February 1980 chose the first Parliament of Zimbabwe: 20 White Roll constituencies on 14 February and 80 Common Roll seats in eight districts on 27 to 29 February; independence followed on 18 April 1980.

classes.note: Put to the registered (largely European) electorate: responsible government or union with South Africa (27 October 1922, before the colony; responsible government won), sweepstakes under legislative control (early 1934, by post), joining the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland (9 April 1953), the 1961 Constitution (26 July 1961), independence under the 1961 Constitution (5 November 1964; the chiefs were consulted separately at the Domboshawa indaba, not by ballot), the republic and the 1969 Constitution (two questions, 20 June 1969), and the majority-rule Constitution of 1979 (30 January 1979, white electorate).

classes.name_en: Legislative Council of Southern Rhodesia, elected members (1899-1923)
classes.locator: https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/written-answers/1922/may/22/referendum-southern-rhodesia (voters qualified to vote for the election of members of the Legislative Council)
classes.disposition_reason: Held under the British South Africa Company administration before the colony; returns were published in the Company's Government Gazette, which is not online, and the National Archives of Zimbabwe could not be reached from here.
classes.note: Elected members sat with nominated Company officials under the Southern Rhodesia Order in Council of 1898; the elected members became a majority from 1907. Elections roughly every three years from 1899 to 1914 and in 1920. Years below are not yet confirmed from an official record.

classes.disposition_reason: Senators were chosen by electoral colleges of members of the House of Assembly and of the Council of Chiefs, or appointed; there was no popular ballot.
classes.note: The 1980 Senate was chosen on 19 March 1980.

classes.disposition_reason: Ward results were declared by each municipality and printed in local newspapers and municipal reports, none of which is online; no colony-wide record of local elections is reachable from here.
classes.note: Salisbury, Bulawayo, Umtali, Gwelo, and other municipalities elected ward councillors on ratepayers' rolls; African councils and township advisory boards were partly elected under separate legislation.
